In summary, our research is concerned with
the assembly of empty capsid particles from FMDV capsid proteins, and the use of these particles in diagnostic assays.
the development of a novel FMDV empty-capsid-based vaccine, which is expressed within the same cells that express the 3C proteases required for their assembly.
the development of a new, efficient system for the production of FMDV empty particles in a mammalian system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the expression of FMDV P1-2AmIRES-3c, in which the 3Cpro expression is dependent on a mutant IRES, is a useful strategy to reduce the toxicity of 3Cpro, and thereby to improve the yield of processed VP0, VP3 and VP1, which self-assemble into empty capsid-like particles.

the expression levels of 3C and the capsid proteins can be controlled by using the appropriate IRES and 3C mutant and that the resulting capsid proteins assemble into empty capsid structures that are similar to the authentic virion.

the use of a mutant IRES to control the relative expression levels of the structural proteins and 3C proteases, and the use of a less catalytically active 3C proteolytic enzyme, can significantly improve the yield of processed FMDV capsid proteins and empty capsid particles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of a mutant 3c(pro) with reduced activity and a dicistronic construct with a mutant 3' UTR IRES element can be used to produce large quantities of processed capsid polypeptides and empty capsids within mammalian cells.

the expression of 3C in the same bicistronic construct as P1- 2A is not detrimental to the production of empty capsid particles in mammalian cells, and that the use of a mutant 3 Cpro and/or a mutant IRES in the bicistronic construct may enhance the yield of processed P1-2 capsid proteins.

the expression of the P1- 2A-mIres-3C cassettes, with the 3 C(pro) activity reduced relative to the level of P1-2a, and using a mutant IRES with low efficiency, produces high levels of processed capsid protein that self-assemble into empty capsid-like particles with a similar morphology to those produced in insect cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the expression of 3Cpro from a dicistronic mRNA, with the expression of 2A and capsid proteins from a monocistronic mRNA, results in a significant increase in the yield of capsid proteins and the formation of empty capsid particles.

the use of a mutant 3c(pro) with reduced activity, together with the use of a dicistronic construct with the 3c(pro)-expressing cassette under the control of a mutant IRES, allows the efficient production of processed capsid protein and the formation of empty capsid particles that retain the ability to interact with cellular receptors.
it is possible to produce large amounts, in a single round of replication, of empty capsid particles from a P1-2AmIRES-3c construct within mammalian cells.
